summary: Anna M. Shields is a sinologist who held posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and Princeton University (~2015).

Anna Madelyn Hennessey specializes in sinology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara, under the doctoral supervision of William F. Powell (attested 2011).

Anna Sawerthal is a tibetologist. She completed an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Johanna Buß, and earned a PhD at the University of Heidelberg under Birgit Kellner and Roland Wenzlhuemer, also studying under Dawa Tsering and Norbu Tashi.

Anna Seidel was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Munich, Hamburg, and under Maxime Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein. Her posts included the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1969) and the Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1969–1991).

Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (PhD). She held posts at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (~1978–1990), UCLA (~1990–1998), and New York University (~1998).

Anna-Pya Sjödin is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Uppsala University in 2007 under the supervision of Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada.

Anne Carolyn Klein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, tibetology, and religious studies. She earned degrees from Binghamton, Wisconsin-Madison, and a PhD from Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. She held posts at Harvard and Rice University (~1987).

Anne E. Monius was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She completed undergraduate, master's, and doctoral degrees at Harvard, studying under Diana L. Eck. She held faculty posts at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) and Harvard (2002).

Anne Feldhaus is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied at Manhattanville University (~1967–1971) and earned a doctoral degree from the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976), later serving as a professor at Arizona State University from 1981.

Anne Hardgrove is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Carleton College (~1987–1991) and the University of Michigan (~1992–1999), and held a post at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.

Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago (~1990–1996) and served as an Assistant Professor of Religion at Cornell University (~1999–2004).

Anne MacDonald is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and tibetology who studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida. She held posts at the University of Hamburg, University of Vienna (attested 2001–2008), and Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2012).

Anne Nishimura Morse specializes in Japanology and history/archaeology. She received her PhD from Harvard University under John M. Rosenfield (attested 2009) and held appointments at Smith College, Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties, Nara National Museum, and Kyoto National Museum.
Anne Ruth Hansen works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She studied under Charles Hallisey and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (attested 2007).

Anne-Marie Blondeau is a scholar of tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein, Dagpo Rinpoche, Yonten Gyatso, and Geshe Ngawang Dakpa. She held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 1982, 2003).

Anne-Marie Esnoul was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Masson-Oursel. She held posts at the CNRS (attested 1947), Institut de civilisation indienne, and EPHE.
Annegret Bollée was a linguist who pursued her studies at Aix-Marseille University, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Bonn (1969).

Annemarie Schimmel was a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She studied at the universities of Berlin and Marburg, and held professorial posts at Marburg (1946, 1953–1954), Ankara University (1954–1967), and Harvard University (1967–1992).

Annemarie von Gabain was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and sinology. She studied at the University of Berlin (~1920–1925), later holding posts there (~1938–1945) and at the University of Hamburg (~1950–1966).

Annette Baier was a philosopher who studied at the University of Otago (~1948–1952) and Somerville College, Oxford (PhD 1952). She held academic posts at Carnegie Mellon University (~1968–1973) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1974–1995).
